title: Testing Cellular Immunity: Interferon-γ Release Assays for TB
summary: Link CD4/CD8 T-cell recognition to interferon-γ release, see why ESAT-6 and CFP-10 let IGRAs ignore BCG, compare QuantiFERON and T-SPOT.TB, and avoid indeterminate and pre-analytical errors.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 46 Hits 2 and 8 (first lesson for Ch. 46). Checked against Zarei 2026 and Pai 2014 (read via a page-fetch tool, first 100,000 characters). Not taught as fact: ELISPOT sensitivity of 1 in 10⁵–10⁶ cells, the two-signal model, cytokine type 1/2 lists, NK mechanisms, NBT percentages, cell-cycle figures, stimulation-index formula, the “never lithium heparin” rule (IGRA kit inserts govern tube types), CD4 diurnal variation, cancer CD4/CD8 ratios, gating rules, microlymphocytotoxicity.

objectives: Explain which T cells recognize class I vs class II and how memory T cells release IFN-γ.
Explain why IGRAs are unaffected by BCG and what they cannot tell you.
Compare QuantiFERON and T-SPOT.TB and recognize indeterminate and pre-analytical errors.

scenes.title: A BCG scar and a positive skin test
scenes.altText: Invented case: a newly hired hospital worker, BCG-vaccinated at birth, has a positive tuberculin skin test (TST) at pre-employment screening; no symptoms; chest film normal. Occupational health orders an interferon-γ release assay (IGRA). The blood sat at room temperature for 14 hours before incubation. Question token: “Can an IGRA separate BCG from TB infection — and can this sample be trusted?”

cues.text: A new hospital worker, vaccinated with BCG at birth, has a positive tuberculin skin test. No symptoms, normal chest film.
An interferon-gamma release assay is ordered, but the blood sat for 14 hours before it was incubated.
Can this test tell BCG from tuberculosis infection, and can the sample be trusted?

props.label: BCG vs TB? Trust the sample?

scenes.title: T-cell memory and interferon-γ
scenes.altText: Presentation card (Zarei 2026): HLA class II (DP, DQ, DR) presents antigens from outside the cell to CD4⁺ helper T cells; HLA class I (A, B, C) presents intracellular peptides to CD8⁺ cytotoxic T cells. Memory card (Pai 2014, read via a page-fetch tool): IGRAs stimulate a patient’s blood T cells with Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens — early secreted antigenic target 6 (ESAT-6) and culture filtrate protein 10 (CFP-10) — and measure the interferon-γ (IFN-γ) released by previously sensitized T cells. Schematic: antigen-presenting cell → T cell → IFN-γ.

cues.text: Helper T cells, which carry CD4, recognize antigen presented on HLA class II; cytotoxic T cells, which carry CD8, recognize peptides on HLA class I.
After an infection, some T cells remember the microbe. Meeting its antigens again, they release cytokines such as interferon-gamma.
An interferon-gamma release assay uses that memory. Fresh blood is mixed with two tuberculosis antigens, ESAT-6 and CFP-10.
If the person has been sensitized to tuberculosis, their T cells release interferon-gamma, which the assay measures.

props.label: Memory T cells → IFN-γ on re-exposure

scenes.title: Why BCG does not fool an IGRA
scenes.altText: Specificity card (Pai 2014): ESAT-6 and CFP-10 are NOT encoded in the genomes of any BCG vaccine strain or of most nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) — so prior BCG vaccination does not make an IGRA positive. Limitation card (Pai 2014): IGRAs CANNOT distinguish latent TB infection from active TB disease. Indeterminate card (Pai 2014): an indeterminate result can occur when the response to the positive (mitogen) control is low; indeterminate proportions were higher in patients with CD4⁺ T-cell counts below 200.

cues.text: Here is why IGRAs help after BCG. ESAT-6 and CFP-10 are not made by any BCG vaccine strain, nor by most nontuberculous mycobacteria.
So BCG vaccination by itself should not make an IGRA positive, which is why it helps in vaccinated people.
But an IGRA only shows T-cell memory. It cannot tell latent infection from active disease.
And the test needs working T cells. If the mitogen control barely responds, as is more common with CD4 counts below 200, the result is indeterminate, not negative.

props.label: Cannot separate latent from active TB

scenes.title: Two formats, and the pre-analytical traps
scenes.altText: Format card (Pai 2014): QuantiFERON — ELISA; IFN-γ reported in IU/mL after subtracting the negative (nil) control; CDC serial-testing guidance uses a cut-off of ≥ 0.35 IU/mL. T-SPOT.TB — ELISPOT; reported as the number of IFN-γ-producing T cells (spot-forming cells). Both include a negative (nil) and a positive (mitogen) control. Pre-analytical card (Pai 2014): incubation DELAY has a negative effect on results; vigorous SHAKING increased IFN-γ in the nil and TB-antigen tubes; blood VOLUME in the antigen tube related inversely to response; some lots were affected by shipping temperature. Variability card: results close to the cut-off can be discordant on repeat (conversions/reversions). Hook answers: an IGRA can separate BCG from TB sensitization; the 14-hour delay can lower the response — recollect and incubate promptly per the kit insert.

cues.text: There are two commercial formats. QuantiFERON is an ELISA that reports interferon-gamma in international units per millilitre, after subtracting the nil tube.
T-SPOT.TB is an ELISPOT that counts individual T cells releasing interferon-gamma, as spots. Both have a nil and a mitogen control.
Handling changes results. Delays before incubation lower the response; vigorous shaking raised interferon-gamma in nil and antigen tubes; blood volume and shipping temperature matter too.

Values near the cut-off can flip on repeat testing. For our worker, the IGRA can separate BCG from TB, but the 14-hour delay may lower the result. Recollect and incubate promptly, following the kit insert.

props.label: Hook: IGRA separates BCG · recollect, incubate promptly

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “A positive IGRA means active TB” (✓ IGRAs cannot distinguish latent infection from active disease); “BCG vaccination makes the IGRA positive” (✓ ESAT-6/CFP-10 are absent from all BCG strains); “Indeterminate = negative” (✓ low mitogen response — consider immunosuppression or handling; it is not a negative).

cues.text: Trap one: a positive IGRA means active tuberculosis. No: it shows T-cell sensitization and cannot separate latent infection from active disease.
Trap two: BCG vaccination makes the IGRA positive. No: the test antigens are not encoded by any BCG strain.
Trap three: an indeterminate result is a negative. No: it usually means the mitogen control failed, from immunosuppression or handling.

props.title: ✗ “IGRA positive = active TB.”
lines: ✓ Latent and active look the same

scenes.title: TB’s ID cards
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “ESAT-6 and CFP-10 are TB’s ID CARDS — BCG never carries them. An IGRA asks memory T cells: ‘Have you seen these cards before?’ The mitogen tube checks the T cells can answer at all.” Tokens: ESAT-6/CFP-10 = TB ID · mitogen = can T cells answer? · memory ≠ active disease. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: ESAT-6 and CFP-10 are tuberculosis’s ID cards, and BCG never carries them. The IGRA asks memory T cells whether they have seen these cards before; the mitogen tube checks the T cells can answer at all.
Where it breaks: a few nontuberculous mycobacteria do carry these antigens; memory says nothing about whether disease is latent or active; and results near the cut-off can flip on repeat testing.

props.title: Where it breaks
lines: A few NTM carry the antigens

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “IGRA: ESAT-6/CFP-10 → IFN-γ from memory T cells · absent from BCG · cannot separate latent from active TB · low mitogen = indeterminate”, “QFT = ELISA IU/mL (≥ 0.35) · T-SPOT = ELISPOT spots · delay lowers, shaking raises”.

cues.text: Interferon-gamma release assays detect T-cell memory of ESAT-6 and CFP-10, antigens absent from BCG, so they separate vaccination from TB sensitization but cannot tell latent from active disease and must be handled promptly to avoid false results.

props.label: ESAT-6/CFP-10 not in BCG · latent ≈ active · low mitogen = indeterminate
QFT ELISA IU/mL · T-SPOT ELISPOT spots · delay ↓ · shaking ↑

explanation.what: Plain language: an IGRA asks whether a person’s T cells “remember” tuberculosis by exposing their blood to two TB proteins and measuring the signal chemical, interferon-gamma, that remembering cells release. Scientific terms: CD4/CD8, HLA class I/II, memory T cell, interferon-γ, ESAT-6, CFP-10, BCG, nontuberculous mycobacteria, latent TB infection, ELISA, ELISPOT, spot-forming cells, nil and mitogen controls, indeterminate result.
explanation.why: ESAT-6 and CFP-10 are encoded by M. tuberculosis but not by BCG strains or most NTM, so only TB-sensitized T cells respond. Both latent infection and active disease leave sensitized T cells, so the test cannot separate them. Without functional T cells (low mitogen response) no conclusion is possible.
explanation.measure: QuantiFERON: IFN-γ IU/mL minus nil (CDC serial-testing cut-off ≥ 0.35 IU/mL); T-SPOT.TB: spot-forming cells; both with nil and mitogen controls (Pai 2014). Pre-analytics: prompt incubation, avoid vigorous shaking, correct blood volume, controlled shipping temperature.
explanation.differs: IGRA antigens (TB-specific; absent from BCG); QuantiFERON (ELISA, concentration) vs T-SPOT.TB (ELISPOT, cell count); negative vs indeterminate (failed mitogen control).
explanation.examAngle: Expect: explain why BCG does not affect an IGRA, state that a positive IGRA does not mean active TB, interpret an indeterminate result, and identify handling errors.

mnemonic.text: ESAT-6 and CFP-10 are TB’s ID CARDS — BCG never carries them. An IGRA asks memory T cells: ‘Have you seen these cards before?’ The mitogen tube checks the T cells can answer at all.
mnemonic.explanation: Specific antigens, memory response and the positive control in one image.
mnemonic.limitation: A few NTM carry the antigens; latent vs active not separated; near-cut-off results can flip.

questions.stem: Why does prior BCG vaccination not cause a positive IGRA?

options.text: Its antigens, ESAT-6 and CFP-10, are not encoded by any BCG strain
options.rationale: Correct. BCG vaccination therefore does not cause a positive IGRA.

options.text: It distinguishes latent from active TB
options.rationale: Incorrect. IGRAs cannot make this distinction.

options.text: It detects antibodies against M. tuberculosis
options.rationale: Incorrect. IGRAs measure T-cell IFN-γ release, not antibodies.
Incorrect. A mitogen positive control is part of the test.

questions.stem: An IGRA from a patient with a CD4 count of 120/μL shows a very low mitogen response and no TB-antigen response. How should it be reported?

options.rationale: Correct. A low mitogen response prevents interpretation; indeterminate results are more common with CD4 < 200.
Incorrect. Without a working positive control, a negative cannot be trusted.
Incorrect. There is no TB-antigen response.
Incorrect. IGRAs never diagnose active TB.

questions.stem: A QuantiFERON tube set was shaken vigorously before incubation. What effect was reported?

options.text: Increased IFN-γ in the nil and TB-antigen tubes
options.rationale: Correct. Pai 2014 reports that vigorous shaking significantly increased IFN-γ responses.

options.text: It converts the assay to an ELISPOT
options.rationale: Incorrect. The format does not change.

options.text: It removes the need for a nil tube
options.rationale: Incorrect. The nil control is still required.
